I have to be especially careful because you never know what can happen next
The event happened because of the way I acted

issues.item: Body Shame: I feel ashamed of what happened to my body
issues.explanation: For a 19-year-old male with stalking trauma, body-focused shame is hard to reconcile unless there was physical or sexual assault. With the given trauma type, this item is clinically incongruent and stands out from the other appraisal items, which are otherwise plausible for stalking.

issues.item: Emotional Numbness: I feel dead inside
issues.explanation: Within Negative Appraisals, 'Betrayal' is hard to reconcile with the validated trauma type of stalking unless the stalker was also a trusted person. Because trauma type has already been fixed as stalking and no other node supplies context supporting an intimate or trusted-perpetrator stalking scenario, this item is clinically questionable in this profile.

issues.item: Character Blame: The event happened to me because of the sort of person I am
issues.explanation: For a stalking trauma, 'betrayal by someone I trusted' can fit only if the stalker was a trusted person, but the profile gives no other items in Triggers, Memory, Threat, or Strategies to support an interpersonal-betrayal formulation. Paired with global characterological self-blame, this creates a specific relational-trauma narrative that is not otherwise represented in the self-report.

issues.item: Betrayal: I was betrayed by someone I trusted
issues.explanation: For a stalking trauma, 'betrayal by someone I trusted' is not impossible, but it implies the stalker was a trusted close other. The rest of the profile provides no supporting items in Memory, Threat, Triggers, or Strategies, and with no active formulation edges this appraisal stands as an unsupported trauma-specific claim. The other appraisal items ('I have to be on guard all the time', 'The world is a dangerous place') fit stalking more generically, but the betrayal item makes the node less coherent as a standalone set.

issues.item: Hypervigilance: I have to be on guard all the time
issues.explanation: These two items are not negative appraisals in the usual cognitive sense; they describe ongoing threat monitoring/safety behavior rather than evaluative beliefs. With a formulation showing no active edges and only the Negative Appraisals node populated, selecting predominantly hypervigilance/vigilance items makes the node content misaligned with the intended construct.

vignette: Kofi had always been a private person, but after the stalking incident, he became consumed by an unshakeable sense that the world was a perilous place. It started with small things – constantly looking over his shoulder on the bus ride to work, avoiding certain streets at night, and being extra cautious when meeting new people online for freelance UX design projects. As time passed, this hypervigilance seeped into every aspect of his life. He found himself wondering if he was being watched even in the safety of his own apartment, and the mere sound of footsteps outside his door made him jump. The incident itself still felt like a blur. Kofi had met someone on a dating app, and what initially seemed like a harmless connection quickly escalated into an obsession. The person would show up at his workplace, send him endless messages, and even appear at his favorite coffee shop. Kofi tried to brush it off as an overzealous admirer, but deep down, he knew something was seriously wrong. When the stalker finally disappeared, Kofi was left with a lingering sense of guilt – if only he had been more careful, more discerning, maybe this wouldn't have happened. As a UX designer, Kofi's work required him to be attuned to human behavior and psychological patterns. But now, his professional curiosity felt tainted by an insatiable need for self-protection. He started to see potential threats everywhere – in the way people interacted with each other online, in the design of public spaces, even in the algorithms that governed social media platforms. His once-thriving freelance business began to suffer as he became increasingly withdrawn, turning down projects and avoiding networking events. Kofi's friends and family grew concerned about his growing isolation, but he couldn't shake off the feeling that he was just one misstep away from disaster. He started to doubt his own judgment, wondering if he had inadvertently invited this kind of attention into his life. His usual optimism was replaced by a nagging sense of self-doubt – maybe he wasn't as careful, as aware, or as in control as he thought. As the months went by, Kofi's world shrunk further and further. He stopped attending design meetups, quit his favorite hobby (photography), and even avoided social gatherings with close friends. It was as if he had lost faith in his own ability to navigate the world safely. His online presence, once a source of creative expression, became a liability – every post, every comment, felt like an invitation for potential predators. Kofi's decision to seek help came when he realized that his fear had become all-consuming. He couldn't bear the thought of living in this state of constant vigilance forever, always waiting for the other shoe to drop. As he sat in his dimly lit apartment, surrounded by the familiar comforts of his design work, Kofi finally acknowledged that something needed to change – not just his environment, but his own perception of himself and the world around him.
